Windowed fft based spectral analysis

Source: R/win_fft.R
win_fft.Rd

The win_fft function conducts a windowed spectral analysis based using the fft

Usage

win_fft(
  data = NULL,
  padfac = 5,
  window_size = NULL,
  run_multicore = FALSE,
  n_cores = NULL,
  genplot = FALSE,
  x_lab = c("depth (m)"),
  y_lab = c("frequency cycle/metre"),
  plot_res = 1,
  perc_vis = 0,
  freq_max = NULL,
  freq_min = NULL,
  palette_name = "viridis",
  color_brewer = "viridis",
  keep_editable = FALSE,
  verbose = FALSE,
  dev_new = FALSE,
  colour_brewer = NULL
)

Arguments

data

Record to analyse (matrix or data frame with two columns: depth/time in column 1, proxy value in column 2), evenly sampled (the sampling interval is taken from the first two rows; rows with missing values are removed). Must be given (the NULL default fails). Default=NULL.

padfac

Zero-padding factor of each window (numeric, >= 1): every window is padded with zeros to padfac times its length before the FFT, which gives a finer (interpolated) frequency grid and a smoother spectrum; 1 or less means no padding. Default=5.

window_size

Length of the running window (numeric, > 0, in the depth/time unit of data, several sampling intervals long). A spectrum is computed for a window centred on every sample; at both ends the record is extended by half a window of AR(1) noise with the mean, standard deviation and lag-1 autocorrelation of the first and last half window. Must be given. Default=NULL.

run_multicore

Compute the windows in parallel on several cores (logical, TRUE or FALSE). Default=FALSE.

n_cores

Number of cores used when run_multicore = TRUE (integer; NULL: an automatic, safe number: physical cores minus one, at most 4, and limited by the free memory). Set options(waverider.n_cores = ...) to change the default. A value > 1 also switches on parallel computing. Results do not depend on the number of cores. Default=NULL.

genplot

Plot the matrix chosen with plot_res against depth and frequency, with the mean spectrum and a colour key (logical, TRUE or FALSE); needs freq_min and freq_max. Default=FALSE.

x_lab

Label of the x-axis (depth/time) of the plot (character). Default="depth (m)".

y_lab

Label of the y-axis (frequency) of the plot (character). Default="frequency cycle/metre".

plot_res

Which matrix of the result is plotted (integer, 1 to 9): 1 amplitude, 2 power, 3 phase, 4 frequency uncertainty, 5 AR(1) confidence level (percent), 6 AR(1) fit, 7 AR(1) 90% power level, 8 AR(1) 95% power level, 9 AR(1) 99% power level. Default=1.

perc_vis

Lower cut-off of the colour scale as a quantile of the plotted values (numeric, between 0 and 1): values below this quantile get the lowest colour, e.g. 0.5 shows only the upper half of the values in colour. Default=0.

freq_max

Highest frequency shown in the plot (numeric, in cycles per depth/time unit, at most the Nyquist frequency); required when genplot = TRUE. Default=NULL.

freq_min

Lowest frequency shown in the plot (numeric, in cycles per depth/time unit, > 0); required when genplot = TRUE. Default=NULL.

palette_name

Name of the colour palette of the power (colour) scale, a character string. Which names are valid depends on color_brewer:

  • color_brewer = "grDevices": "rainbow", "heat.colors", "terrain.colors", "topo.colors", "cm.colors", or any of the 115 hcl.colors palettes (list them with grDevices::hcl.pals()), for example "viridis", "Plasma", "Inferno", "YlOrRd", "Spectral", "Blue-Red", "Zissou 1".

  • color_brewer = "viridis": "viridis", "magma", "inferno", "plasma", "cividis", "rocket", "mako", "turbo".

  • color_brewer = "RColorBrewer": "BrBG", "PiYG", "PRGn", "PuOr", "RdBu", "RdGy", "RdYlBu", "RdYlGn", "Spectral", "Accent", "Dark2", "Paired", "Pastel1", "Pastel2", "Set1", "Set2", "Set3", "Blues", "BuGn", "BuPu", "GnBu", "Greens", "Greys", "Oranges", "OrRd", "PuBu", "PuBuGn", "PuRd", "Purples", "RdPu", "Reds", "YlGn", "YlGnBu", "YlOrBr", "YlOrRd" (also listed by wr_brewer_palettes()).

  • color_brewer = "colorRamps": "blue2green", "blue2green2red", "blue2red", "blue2yellow", "cyan2yellow", "green2red", "magenta2green", "matlab.like", "matlab.like2", "ygobb".

  • color_brewer = "scico" (all except "batlowK" need the scico package): "acton", "bam", "bamako", "bamO", "batlow", "batlowK", "batlowW", "berlin", "bilbao", "broc", "brocO", "buda", "bukavu", "cork", "corkO", "davos", "devon", "fes", "glasgow", "grayC", "hawaii", "imola", "lajolla", "lapaz", "lipari", "lisbon", "managua", "navia", "nuuk", "oleron", "oslo", "roma", "romaO", "tofino", "tokyo", "turku", "vanimo", "vik", "vikO".

Low power is drawn with the first colour of the palette and high power with the last. Default="viridis".

color_brewer

Palette family from which palette_name is taken, a character string: "grDevices", "viridis", "RColorBrewer", "colorRamps" or "scico" (the last one, except for "batlowK", needs the scico package). See palette_name for the palette names of each family. Default="viridis".

keep_editable

Keep the graphical parameters and layout after plotting, so that extra features can be added (logical, TRUE or FALSE); FALSE restores the previous settings. Default=FALSE.

verbose

Show a progress bar of the window computations (logical, TRUE or FALSE). Default=FALSE.

dev_new

Open a new plot window (via wr_open_device()) before plotting (logical, TRUE or FALSE); a separate window gives a "nice" looking plot, but in an R markdown document the plot may then not appear. Default=FALSE.

colour_brewer

British spelling of color_brewer, with the same options; if given (not NULL) it overrides color_brewer. Default=NULL.

Value

Returns a list which contains 10 elements element 1: Amplitude matrix element 2: Power matrix element 3: Phase matrix element 4: AR1_CL matrix element 5: AR1_Fit matrix element 6: AR1_90_power matrix element 7: AR1_95_power matrix element 8: AR1_99_power matrix element 9: depth element 10: y_axis If genplot is Default=TRUE then a plot of one of the elements 1:8 is plotted

References

Routines for astrochronologic testing, astronomical time scale construction, and time series analysis <doi:10.1016/j.earscirev.2018.11.015>

Author

Based on the periodogram function of the 'astrochron' R package.

Examples

# \donttest{
#Conduct a windowed ftt on the magnetic susceptibility record
#of the Sullivan core of Pas et al., (2018).

mag_win_fft <- win_fft(data= mag,
                   padfac = 5,
                   window_size = 12.5,
                   run_multicore = FALSE,
                   genplot = FALSE,
                   x_lab = c("depth (m)"),
                   y_lab = c("frequency cycle/metre"),
                   plot_res = 1,
                   perc_vis = 0.5,
                   freq_max = 5,
                   freq_min = 0.001,
                   palette_name ="rainbow",
                   color_brewer= "grDevices",
                   keep_editable=FALSE,
                   verbose=FALSE,
                   dev_new=FALSE)
# }
